## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="x01-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- x01-ideas:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<dl class="lx-ideas"><dt>Disciplines</dt><dd>Power electronics, protection, aerodynamics, combustion, reactor physics, electrochemistry and control each design a part of the system.</dd><dt>What crosses over</dt><dd>A system model borrows ratings, efficiencies, ramp limits, outlet temperatures and failure rates, plus the control room's operating rules.</dd><dt>What stays</dt><dd>Designs, materials and calculations stay with each discipline; the model sees them only through the numbers they lead to.</dd><dt>Cybersecurity</dt><dd>NERC's mandatory standards protect the bulk power system's cyber systems; distribution-grid devices are in general outside them.</dd></dl>
<!-- x01-ideas:end -->
</div>
</div>
<!-- x01-stop:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-card xs-stop" id="x01-stop"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Where we stop</p><h3>This side topic stops at the nameplate</h3><p class="xs-stop-lede">Devices enter the course only as ratings, efficiencies, ramp limits, outlet temperatures and failure rates; designing them belongs to each discipline.</p><div class="xs-stop-cols"><div><h4 class="xs-h">This side topic covers</h4><ul><li>What each discipline designs and which questions it answers.</li><li>Which numbers a system model borrows from it, and where this course uses them.</li><li>Where cybersecurity sits: standards for the bulk power system's control systems.</li></ul></div><div><h4 class="xs-h">Left to specialists</h4><ul><li>Design methods, physics and calculations for any device.</li><li>Testing, certification and equipment standards.</li><li>Running or securing a control room.</li></ul></div></div><h4 class="xs-h">Read next, three rungs</h4><ol class="xs-ladder"><li><b>Start here.</b> A short tour of turbines, generators and inverters, and how each makes electricity. <span class="xs-src"><a href="https://www.eia.gov/energyexplained/electricity/how-electricity-is-generated.php">EIA, Electricity explained: How electricity is generated</a>, read 3 November 2026</span></li><li><b>Go further.</b> Pick one discipline and read its textbook: each component card above names one, in any recent edition. <span class="xs-src">The reading line on each component card, list of 7 November 2026</span></li><li><b>Go deep.</b> For control systems: how the mandatory cybersecurity standards reach the bulk power system, and where distributed resources stand. <span class="xs-src"><a href="https://nerc.com/globalassets/our-work/reports/white-papers/white_paper_cybersecurity_for-ders_and_der_aggregators.pdf">NERC, Cyber Security for Distributed Energy Resources and DER Aggregators (white paper)</a>, December 2022</span></li></ol></div>
<!-- x01-stop:end -->
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Where each borrowed number enters a model</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li><b>Efficiency.</b> A heat rate times a fuel price becomes a running cost per MWh in a dispatch model (<a href="m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html">M1</a>).</li>
<li><b>Ramp limit.</b> It becomes a rule linking one hour's output to the next (<a href="m02-unit-commitment.html">M2</a>).</li>
<li><b>Round trip.</b> It becomes the loss in a storage balance, hour by hour (<a href="m04-storage-multienergy.html">M4</a>).</li>
<li><b>Failure rate.</b> It becomes the chance of a forced outage in an adequacy simulation (<a href="a05-adequacy.html">A5</a>).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

<p class="lx-lede">Two quick checks.</p>
<!-- x01-check:start (written from the data by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="x01-myth"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="design" data-answer="myth"><p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “To plan a grid, a modeller needs the full design of every turbine and inverter.”</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. A system model borrows a few numbers from each design (ratings, efficiencies, ramp limits, outlet temperatures, failure rates); the design itself stays with the engineers.</p></details></div></div><div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="x01"><div class="lx-qq" data-id="eff" data-answer="b"><p class="lx-qtext">U.S. combined-cycle plants burned 7,535 Btu of fuel per kWh in 2025, and one kWh holds 3,412 Btu. About what share of the fuel's energy becomes electricity?</p><ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">About 23%</li><li data-value="b">About 45%</li><li data-value="c">About 68%</li></ul><details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>3,412 ÷ 7,535 = 0.453, about 45%: the efficiency a model borrows as a heat rate (lesson F4).</p></details></div></div>
<!-- x01-check:end -->
